lines: Built with: vite.config.ts, package.json declares @nextcloud/vite-config ^2.3.0, vite ^7.0.0.
Other delivered libraries: 81, axios 1.18.1, micromark 4.0.2, dompurify 3.4.15, mdast-util-to-hast 13.2.1, focus-trap 8.2.2, property-information 7.2.0, and 75 more.
Packages and versions are those the .license files beside the chunks name, since the source maps miss packages through the toolchain defect named here.

Known toolchain defect: vite-plugin-css-injected-by-js 4.0.1 in package-lock.json, where the CSS is injected by JavaScript, puts the code that injects the CSS in front of the chunk without shifting its source map, so the map the bundler combines from it loses sources. Here the map of _plugin-vue_export-helper-VMCav1IU.chunk.mjs names 2 of the 6 packages its .license file names, and 1 further chunk shows the same.
The app runs as built; only the map is short, so the frameworks and libraries are read from the .license files instead.

Built in a copy with @nextcloud/vite-config 3.0.0-beta.1, vite 8.3.5 (vite-plugin-css-injected-by-js 5.0.3), the map of tr-BtTTIrbi.chunk.mjs names 1 of the 2 packages its .license file names still: not fixed.
Every delivered file in js carries a source map, so every byte can be charged to the package and the module it came from.
No package the build delivers is imported by its root in src: every one of the 8 packages it imports is named by the module that is used.
